note: Sunday weekend sweep, 13 Sep 2026 07:02 SGT -- before Asia's Monday open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30) and after Friday 11 Sep's US close. Markets were shut all weekend so items are a mix of confirmed Sat/Sun-dated developments (Hormuz diplomacy, CLARITY Act odds, rare-earth squeeze) and the most decision-relevant items still live from Friday's session (FOMC setup, metals whipsaw, silver deficit, SGX REITs). No genuinely new weekend item was found for SGX banks/REITs or HK tech policy specifically -- both carry the freshest confirmed reads instead.

items.headline: Bahrain refuses to join Monday's Iran-Oman Hormuz talks, fracturing Gulf unity
items.summary: Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said it will not participate in Monday 14 Sep's Oman-hosted meeting between Iran, Gulf states and Iraq on Strait of Hormuz shipping arrangements, citing the absence of restored diplomatic ties with Tehran (severed since 2016) and recent attacks on Bahraini infrastructure. This splits the Gulf response just as Iran pushes for a deal.
items.actionable: A partial Gulf boycott means Monday's framework is more likely a narrow Iran-Oman bilateral shell than a comprehensive fix -- don't expect oil to fully retrace the war premium off this meeting alone.

items.headline: Iran and Oman set to sign partial Hormuz 'safe shipping corridor' deal Monday in Muscat
items.summary: Iran's president said Iran and Oman will sign an agreement Monday establishing a temporary joint shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, to be announced to the IMO alongside regional foreign ministers. Iranian officials caution this is a phased, partial framework -- disputes remain over Iran's push for transit fees, which Oman rejects.
items.actionable: Watch Monday's Muscat signing closely -- a narrow safe-corridor deal without a fee resolution is a partial de-risking event, likely to cap rather than reverse the Hormuz oil premium.

items.headline: FOMC meets Sep 15-16; a 25bp hike is now the base case at ~85-90% priced, not a cut
items.summary: The Fed's next decision lands Wednesday 2pm ET off a current 3.5%-3.75% target range. CME-implied odds of a quarter-point hike jumped to roughly 85-90% after August's hotter-than-expected core CPI, and held firm to slightly higher through the weekend with no new Fed commentary since Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks (28 Aug).
items.actionable: This is the single biggest scheduled catalyst for the whole book this week -- the real surprise risk is a hold, which would likely spark an outsized relief rally in miners and S-REITs given how heavily a hike is already priced.

items.headline: Senate CLARITY Act cloture vote Monday: passage odds collapse from 82% to ~10-16%
items.summary: The Senate's cloture test on the crypto market-structure bill (Mon 15 Sep, needs 60 votes) faces three unresolved fights: ethics rules on Trump's ~$1.4B personal crypto income, DeFi developer liability, and a stablecoin-yield provision threatening roughly $1.35B of Coinbase USDC revenue. Prediction-market odds of 2026 passage have fallen from 82% in February to 10-16% as of early September.
items.actionable: Failure is largely priced in already -- the asymmetric surprise is to the upside if the bill somehow clears 60 votes Monday, the same day FOMC week begins.

items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs log 4th straight day of outflows (~$463M) as Ethereum ETFs take in $216M Friday
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs broke a 3-week inflow streak with four consecutive sessions of net redemptions totaling roughly $463M into the weekend, consistent with the hawkish Fed repricing. Spot Ethereum ETFs moved the opposite way, taking in $216M on Friday alone -- a genuine flow divergence between the two largest crypto ETF complexes.
items.actionable: The BTC/ETH ETF-flow divergence is a real, dated data point worth tracking into FOMC week -- it suggests institutional money is currently rotating within crypto rather than exiting it outright.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export halt to the US and Japan deepens ahead of the Sep 24 Trump-Xi summit
items.summary: Chinese suppliers have refused to ship yttrium, terbium, gallium and indium-phosphide to US buyers since early August after Beijing sanctioned the Responsible Business Alliance; Japan recorded near-zero terbium exports and a 98% yttrium drop (Jan-Aug) versus a year earlier. China still controls roughly 99% of heavy rare-earth processing, so near-term diversification isn't realistic before the summit; analysts expect only a cosmetic, tactical easing around 24 Sep rather than a structural fix.
items.actionable: The squeeze is real and ongoing, not just rhetoric -- treat any pre-summit goodwill gesture from Beijing as tactical, not structural, so the ex-China rare-earth watchlist thesis stays intact even through a possible short-term relief rally.

items.headline: MP Materials short interest at 20.4% of float as rare-earth curbs rally the stock
items.summary: MP Materials shares rallied on China's rare-earth export curbs, with 18 analysts averaging a Strong Buy rating and a 12-month price target of $75.38 (about +47% from early-September levels); short interest sits at 20.4% of MP's available float. Lynas is also rebounding on US-government-backed supply-chain deals.
items.actionable: High short interest means any friendly summit headline (or an actual export resumption) could trigger an outsized squeeze -- worth sizing the watchlist entry with that asymmetry in mind.

items.headline: Gold and silver whipsaw through the CPI print, close near $4,385-4,389 and ~$65 despite 90% hike odds
items.summary: Gold opened Friday at its lowest level in over a month ahead of CPI, then reversed to trade near $4,385-4,389/oz once the headline matched consensus; silver swung between a 2.6% intraday loss and a recovery toward $65. Metals shrugging off a near-90%-priced hike is a constructive tell, but the scale of the intraday whipsaw means Monday's open can gap either way.
items.actionable: Avoid adding leverage to the miners sleeve until Wednesday's FOMC outcome is confirmed -- the whipsaw shows genuine two-sided risk into the decision.

items.headline: S&P snaps four-day losing streak (+0.86% to 7,657) as VIX collapses ~11-12%
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose to roughly 7,657, ending four straight down sessions, while the VIX fell about 11-12% to near 15.6-15.8 as Brent's pullback and easing Treasury yields outweighed the hotter-than-expected core CPI. The move reflects relief that inflation wasn't worse, not resolution of the hike outlook.
items.actionable: The vol collapse is a genuine short-term relief signal, but it coexists with a near-90%-priced hike -- use this calm to review hedges on the large cash pile rather than chasing the rally into FOMC.

items.headline: Strait of Hormuz transit collapses to ~3% of pre-war volume as OSINT trackers flag widening oil backwardation
items.summary: Independent OSINT war trackers report the Strait of Hormuz running at roughly 3% of pre-war transit volume after the Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown removed the alternate southern export route, forcing nearly all Gulf crude through the contested strait. Brent backwardation has widened to roughly $8.3/bbl with WTI holding above $100.
items.actionable: This data is from independent trackers, not wire services, so treat directionally -- but the structural signal (a US SPR drawdown of ~130M bbl over 27 weeks nearing an Oct 1 authority cliff) is a genuine tail risk worth flagging for the cash-pile/inflation-hedge allocation.

items.headline: Silver on track for a sixth straight annual supply deficit; 2026 gap projected near 67 million ounces
items.summary: The silver market is heading for its sixth consecutive year where industrial and investment demand outstrips mine-plus-recycled supply, with the 2026 shortfall projected around 67 million ounces against total supply near 1.05 billion ounces. Mine output fell about 2% in 2026 despite record-high prices because roughly 70% of mined silver is a byproduct of lead/zinc/copper operations.
items.actionable: The structural deficit underpins the long-term case for the silver-miners sleeve independent of this week's Fed-driven volatility -- a reason to hold through the CPI/FOMC noise rather than trade around it.

items.headline: Singapore's REIT sector down 8.2% YTD versus the STI's +24.6% as the market re-prices Fed hikes
items.summary: The FTSE ST All-Share REIT Index is down 8.2% year-to-date as of early September, badly lagging the Straits Times Index's 24.6% gain, as investors shift from pricing Fed cuts to pricing hikes. Analysts still hold an overweight-but-selective stance on S-REITs, favoring names with fixed-rate debt and defensive earnings.
items.actionable: With a Fed hike now ~85-90% priced for Wednesday, expect continued pressure on Keppel REIT/Mapletree PACT-type names until the FOMC outcome is confirmed -- stay selective/defensive rather than adding on dips this week.
